qualitative_feedback: Code organization and documentation are good, but some scripts seem redundant.
Feature engineering is extensive and well-documented.
Model selection and hyperparameter tuning are well-performed.
Usage of SHAP values for interpretability is appreciated.
Presentation and report files are well-structured and informative.
No direct evidence of cloud infrastructure usage is seen in the provided files.
README is comprehensive and easy to follow.
Commit history is not provided, but the overall code structure suggests regular updates.
The repository appears to be focused on data ingestion and EDA, with some data visualization.
No machine learning models are present in the provided code.
The code utilizes pandas and various data manipulation techniques, indicating a focus on data engineering.
Cloud infrastructure is not explicitly utilized, but data is stored locally in parquet format.
Visualizations are created using matplotlib, seaborn, and plotly, indicating a moderate level of visualization complexity.
Communication and documentation are minimal, with only a brief README and some comments in the code.
The project utilizes a declarative pipeline with 'targets' library, which aids in reproducing and maintaining the workflow.
Utilization of 'readabs' and 'readrba' libraries simplifies data acquisition from Australian Bureau of Statistics and Reserve Bank of Australia.
Implementation of a registry for series ID and metadata enhances data handling and traceability.
Employment of 'ggplot2' and other visualization tools helps in creating informative and engaging reports.
Absence of explicit machine learning components, instead relying on statistical methods and data manipulation.
Data pipeline documentation and comments provide clear understanding of the project's workflow and intentions.
Extensive use of Quarto for presentation and reporting, indicating a focus on communication and visualization.
